Single-Sample Taxon Set Enrichment Analysis

Source: R/ssTaxSEA.R
ssTaxSEA.Rd

Computes a per-sample score for each taxon set as the mean centered log-ratio (CLR) of the set's members within that sample.

Usage

ssTaxSEA(
  counts,
  lookup_missing = FALSE,
  min_set_size = 5,
  max_set_size = 300,
  custom_db = NULL,
  pseudocount = NULL,
  scale = c("counts", "proportion"),
  reference = c("all", "top_k"),
  top_k = 20
)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix, data.frame, or SummarizedExperiment/TreeSummarizedExperiment object. For matrix/data.frame input: rows are taxa, columns are samples, and row names must be taxon names (e.g. species names or NCBI IDs). For SummarizedExperiment input: the first assay is used and rownames() provide taxon identifiers.

lookup_missing

Logical indicating whether to fetch missing NCBI IDs via the NCBI API. Default is FALSE.

min_set_size

Minimum size of taxon sets to include. Default is 5.

max_set_size

Maximum size of taxon sets to include. Default is 300.

custom_db

A user-provided list of taxon sets. If NULL (default), the built-in TaxSEA database is used (excluding BugSigDB).

pseudocount

Numeric value added to every value before the log transform, to handle zeros. It is on the scale set by scale: if NULL (default), 0.5 for scale = "counts" and 1e-6 for scale = "proportion". This choice affects the scores, so report it alongside your results.

scale

Either "counts" (default) or "proportion". With "counts" the input is used as supplied and must be counts or another count-like measure. With "proportion" each sample is first divided by its total, so counts, proportions and percentages (for example MetaPhlAn output) are all accepted, and pseudocount is a proportion. See Details.

reference

Either "all" (default) or "top_k". What each sample's log values are centered on: the mean over all taxa (the standard CLR), or the mean over that sample's top_k most abundant detected taxa. See Details.

top_k

Number of most abundant detected taxa used as the reference when reference = "top_k". Default is 20. A sample with fewer detected taxa uses all of its detected taxa.

Value

A numeric matrix of scores with taxon sets as rows and samples as columns. Higher values indicate that the set's members are more abundant in that sample, relative to the average taxon in that same sample (or, with reference = "top_k", relative to that sample's most abundant taxa).

Details

For each sample the counts are centered log-ratio transformed, and the score for a taxon set is the mean of the CLR values of the set's members:

$$score_{S,j} = \frac{1}{|S|} \sum_{i \in S} clr_{ij}$$

The CLR is computed across all taxa supplied in counts, before any subsetting to set members. This matters: restricting the matrix to set members first would make the geometric mean that the CLR divides by depend on the sets being tested, which manufactures apparent signal in sets that have none.

Because the score is a within-sample quantity, ssTaxSEA does not need a cohort and is well defined for a single sample.

Choosing a reference

The standard CLR (reference = "all") centers each sample on the mean log value of every taxon in the table, zeros included. That reference moves with richness: when many rare taxa drop out, as after antibiotics or chemotherapy, the reference falls and every surviving taxon's score rises, even if its abundance relative to the other survivors has not changed. Many taxon sets share the same surviving members, so hundreds of scores can rise together. Adjusting for richness in a downstream model does not remove this. The reference also depends on which rows are in the table, so filtering taxa differently changes every score.

reference = "top_k" centers each sample on the mean log value of its top_k most abundant detected taxa. Rare taxa are still scored and still count towards their sets; they just no longer move everyone else's score. Losing rare taxa, or adding or removing rare and all-zero rows, leaves the reference unchanged. Zeros never enter the reference: a sample with fewer than top_k detected taxa uses all of them. The score then reads as abundance relative to the sample's dominant taxa.

A pseudocount set from each sample's own data would move with the rare tail in the same way, which is why pseudocount is a fixed value. On the count scale a pseudocount of 0.5 reads is a different proportion in samples of different depth; scale = "proportion" with a small fixed pseudocount avoids that. The default of 1e-6 is near the detection limit of deep shotgun profiles; raise it if your smallest detected proportions are larger. For relative abundance input, such as MetaPhlAn percentages, use scale = "proportion".

Interpreting the scores

Scores are comparable across samples within a taxon set: a higher score in sample A than sample B means the set's members make up more of sample A's community.

Scores are not comparable across taxon sets. A set of abundant taxa will score higher than a set of rare taxa in every sample, regardless of biology, simply because its members are more abundant. When visualising the matrix, center or scale the rows first (for example t(scale(t(scores)))), and when comparing groups, compare a single set's scores between groups rather than comparing different sets to each other.

No p-values are returned. The score is a descriptive statistic; to test a hypothesis, compare scores across samples using a test appropriate to your design (for example wilcox.test or a linear model on one row of the returned matrix).

See also

TaxSEA for group-level enrichment.

Examples

# Toy count matrix: 30 taxa x 8 samples
set.seed(42)
counts <- matrix(rpois(240, lambda = 10), nrow = 30, ncol = 8)
rownames(counts) <- paste0("Taxon_", seq_len(30))
colnames(counts) <- paste0("Sample_", seq_len(8))

# Raise one set's members in the last four samples
counts[1:6, 5:8] <- counts[1:6, 5:8] * 5

sets <- list(
  elevated_set = paste0("Taxon_", 1:6),
  control_set  = paste0("Taxon_", 20:27)
)

scores <- ssTaxSEA(counts, custom_db = sets, min_set_size = 3)
dim(scores)        # sets x samples
#> [1] 2 8
round(scores, 2)
#>              Sample_1 Sample_2 Sample_3 Sample_4 Sample_5 Sample_6 Sample_7
#> elevated_set     0.02     0.20     0.04    -0.13     1.15     1.37     1.31
#> control_set     -0.09     0.02     0.01    -0.01    -0.29    -0.34    -0.52
#>              Sample_8
#> elevated_set     1.07
#> control_set     -0.14

# The planted signal shows up as higher scores in samples 5-8
rowMeans(scores[, 1:4]) - rowMeans(scores[, 5:8])
#> elevated_set  control_set 
#>   -1.1948884    0.3033688 

# A reference that is not moved by changes in rare taxa, for
# relative abundance input
pct <- sweep(counts, 2, colSums(counts), "/") * 100
ssTaxSEA(pct, custom_db = sets, min_set_size = 3,
         scale = "proportion", reference = "top_k", top_k = 10)
#>                Sample_1    Sample_2   Sample_3   Sample_4   Sample_5   Sample_6
#> elevated_set -0.2824106 -0.09203292 -0.2866433 -0.5232409  0.4322547  0.5063751
#> control_set  -0.3933116 -0.28047262 -0.3170458 -0.3956802 -1.0473972 -1.2533668
#>                Sample_7   Sample_8
#> elevated_set  0.4450376  0.3641358
#> control_set  -1.4454834 -0.8702312
